name: refactor_python_class_to_dataclass
description: Refactors a boilerplate class (init/eq/repr) into a dataclass preserving fields, equality and repr
prompts: The Point class in point.py hand-writes __init__, __eq__ and __repr__. Refactor it to use the @dataclass decorator (from dataclasses) instead of the boilerplate methods. Preserve behavior exactly: the fields are x, y, and label (label defaults to "origin"); two Points are equal iff all three fields are equal; and repr(Point(1, 2, "x")) must remain "Point(x=1, y=2, label='x')". Keep the class name Point.

files.point.py:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Point:
    x: int
    y: int
    # DRIFT: label no longer participates in equality.
    label: str = field(default="origin", compare=False)
